places.name: Giant Panda National Park
places.tagline: Some 22,000 km² of bamboo forest across the Minshan, Qionglai and Qinling ranges, home to roughly 1,300 of the world's ~1,900 wild pandas.
places.access: Gateways from Chengdu: **Wolong/Shenshuping** (2.5 h by road via Dujiangyan), **Dujiangyan** (HSR 35 min), **Bifengxia/Ya'an** (fast rail ~1 h), **Labahe** (Tianquan).
places.best_for: Wild forest, rhododendrons, red pandas, quiet trails
description: Established in 2021, the park joins dozens of older reserves into one protected landscape. It is huge, steep and mostly wild. Visitor infrastructure is limited to a few gateways, which is exactly why it's quiet.

Be realistic: **you will almost certainly not see a wild panda.** Researchers go years without one. Come for the cloud forest, mossy gorges, golden snub-nosed monkeys (if lucky), red pandas and the feeling of wilderness 2 hours from a megacity. See the pandas themselves at a breeding base inside the park (Shenshuping, Dujiangyan Panda Valley, Bifengxia).
highlights: Shenshuping (Wolong) breeding base: pandas in big forested enclosures
Labahe and Erlangshan: cloud forest, hot springs, few foreign visitors
Spring bamboo shoots draw pandas to lower slopes in April–May
places.april: Rhododendrons and fresh bamboo. Mild in the valleys (15–20 °C daytime), cold and possibly snowy above 3,000 m. Showers are common.
places.health: Most visitor areas are at 1,000–2,500 m, but roads to the western side (e.g. Balang Shan towards Siguniang) cross 3,800 m+. Turn on the altitude layer.

places.name: Wolong & Shenshuping Panda Base
places.name_zh: 卧龙中华大熊猫苑神树坪基地
places.tagline: Pandas in steep, forested enclosures in a deep mountain valley: the antidote to the crowded Chengdu base.
places.time_needed: 1 day, better 2 with a night in Wolong
places.access: Car/driver or bus from Chengdu via Dujiangyan, 2.5–3 h. Combine with Siguniang (another 2 h west).
places.best_for: Seeing pandas without crowds; a stop on the way to Siguniang
description: Wolong was the historic heart of panda research (George Schaller worked here in the 1980s). The 2008 earthquake destroyed the old centre, and **Shenshuping** is the rebuilt base: fewer visitors, more natural enclosures, cubs in spring.
The valley road continues over Balang Shan to Mount Siguniang, one of the great mountain drives in China.
places.crowd_tips: Weekdays are calm. Arrive before 10:00 when pandas are most active (feeding).
places.april: Pleasant, green; pandas active in the cooler mornings.
places.health: Base at ~1,850 m is fine. The road west over Balang Shan reaches ~3,850 m at the tunnel; that's fine to drive through, just don't sleep up there.

places.name: Chengdu Panda Breeding Base
places.name_zh: 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地
places.tagline: Guaranteed pandas, guaranteed crowds. Go at opening time or skip it for Shenshuping.
places.access: Metro + shuttle bus, ~40 min from central Chengdu. Book timed tickets in advance (passport needed).
places.best_for: Easy panda fix if short on time
description: Beautifully landscaped and very well run, with dozens of pandas including cubs. It's also one of the most visited attractions in China, and the walkways around the popular enclosures can be shoulder-to-shoulder by 10:00.
places.crowd_tips: Be at the gate at opening (7:30); go straight to the far enclosures first. Avoid weekends, Qingming and 1–5 May at all costs.
places.april: Spring cubs on display; pandas sleep once it warms up after ~10:00.

places.name: Mount Siguniang (Four Girls Mountain)
places.tagline: Alpine valleys, yaks, Tibetan villages and a 6,250 m peak, 4–5 hours from Chengdu.
places.access: Bus or driver from Chengdu via Wolong and the Balang Shan tunnel (4–5 h). Base yourself in Rilong town.
places.best_for: Multi-day hiking, Tibetan culture, big mountains
description: Three valleys fan out from Rilong: **Shuangqiao** (bus road, easy sightseeing), **Changping** (boardwalk + trail to Mushroom Mountain, the classic hike) and **Haizi** (horses/trekking to alpine lakes at the foot of the peaks, often done as a 2-day trek with camping).
Feels like a Himalayan trip in miniature, and still far less visited than Jiuzhaigou.
highlights: Balang Shan pass views on the drive in
places.april: Late snow on high trails, valleys just turning green, nights below freezing. Late April is better than early April.
places.health: **Everything here is above 3,000 m. Rilong town, where you sleep, is ~3,200 m.** Not advisable in pregnancy without your doctor's OK; acclimatise if not pregnant.

places.name: Mount Emei
places.tagline: Sacred Buddhist mountain: monasteries, cloud seas, cheeky macaques, and a 3,000 m gilded summit.
places.access: HSR Chengdu → Emeishan (1–1.5 h), then bus to Baoguo Temple. Combine with the Leshan Giant Buddha (20 min away).
places.best_for: Temple-hopping hike, sunrise above the clouds
description: One of China's four sacred Buddhist mountains and a UNESCO site. The summit (cable car + bus) is a circus, but the stepped trails between **Wannian Temple, Qingyin Pavilion and Xixiang Chi** run through subtropical forest with far fewer people.
Stay a night in a monastery guesthouse for the atmosphere.
places.crowd_tips: Walk the lower and middle trails; take the bus/cable car only for the summit. Avoid weekends.
places.april: Lush and green below, possibly icy at the summit, often in cloud.
places.health: The Golden Summit is ~3,080 m. A day visit by cable car is common; **for pregnancy, sleep low** (Baoguo / Wannian ~1,000 m).

places.name: Tiger Leaping Gorge High Trail
places.tagline: One of the world's deepest gorges, with the Yangtze roaring 2 km below a guesthouse-to-guesthouse trail.
places.access: From Lijiang: bus/driver to Qiaotou (~2 h). The Lijiang–Shangri-La railway (opened 2023) has a Hutiaoxia station near Qiaotou.
places.best_for: Classic 2-day trek with comfortable guesthouses
description: The high trail runs ~22 km from Qiaotou to Tina's Guesthouse along the north side of the gorge, with the 5,500 m Jade Dragon and Haba snow mountains on either side. Guesthouses (Naxi Family, Tea Horse, Halfway) make it a no-camping trek with spectacular terraces for dinner.
Day 2 can include the steep descent to the river at Middle Tiger Leaping Stone.
highlights: Middle Gorge descent to the rapids
places.crowd_tips: Popular with backpackers but spread over 22 km. Weekdays are mellow.
places.april: Dry and sunny, ~20 °C days; good season, before monsoon rockfall risk.
places.health: The trail tops out around 2,670 m at the 28 Bends; **guesthouses sit at ~2,000–2,300 m**, below the 2,500 m threshold. Steep, exposed sections in places.

places.name: Shaxi
places.tagline: The last intact Tea Horse Road market town: a sleepy Bai valley that Dali and Lijiang used to be.
places.access: From Dali (~2 h by car/bus) or from Jianchuan on the Dali–Lijiang railway (45 min taxi).
places.best_for: Slow travel, cycling, village walks, Friday market
description: Sideng Square, with its theatre stage, temple and caravan inns, was restored by a Swiss–Chinese project in the 2000s and won a World Monuments Fund listing. Around it: rice fields, Bai villages and the **Shibaoshan** grottoes and temples (a beautiful half-day hike).
It has become trendier (cafés, boutique guesthouses), but compared to Lijiang it's blissfully quiet.
places.crowd_tips: Weekdays are very quiet. The Friday market brings Yi and Bai villagers from the hills.
places.april: Dry season, sunny, ~22 °C days, cool nights (~7 °C). Rapeseed fields may still be in flower early in the month.

places.name: Meili Snow Mountains & Yubeng
places.tagline: Sacred Kawagebo (6,740 m, never climbed) and a car-free Tibetan village reached only on foot.
places.access: Rail Lijiang → Shangri-La (2023), then bus/driver to Deqin/Feilaisi (4–5 h). Trek into Yubeng from Xidang (or ride a mule).
places.best_for: A real trekking adventure; Tibetan Buddhism
description: Kawagebo is one of Tibetan Buddhism's holiest peaks; a 1991 Sino-Japanese expedition ended in an avalanche that killed 17 and climbing was later banned. **Yubeng village** sits in a hidden valley beneath it, with treks to the Ice Lake, the Sacred Waterfall and Shennu meadows.
Far from the train network and high, but probably the most spectacular place on any Yunnan itinerary.
places.april: Clear mornings, snow on passes, rhododendrons in bloom lower down. Cold nights.
places.health: **High altitude throughout: Feilaisi ~3,400 m, Yubeng ~3,000–3,200 m, the Nazongla pass ~3,700 m, Ice Lake ~3,900 m.** Not suitable during pregnancy.

places.name: Yuanyang Hani Rice Terraces
places.tagline: Thousands of mirror-like terraces carved over 1,300 years by the Hani, filling entire mountainsides.
places.access: From Jianshui or Mengzi (fast rail from Kunming) by bus/driver, 2.5–3 h. Stay in Duoyishu or Pugaolao villages.
places.best_for: Photography, village walks, minority cultures
description: UNESCO World Heritage since 2013. The viewpoints (**Duoyishu** for sunrise, **Bada** and **Laohuzui** for sunset) are spectacular, but the real joy is walking the paths between Hani villages with their mushroom-roofed houses and morning markets.
Few foreign visitors and a strong local culture make it a strong candidate for the 'authentic' part of the trip.
places.crowd_tips: Photographers gather at Duoyishu at sunrise. Walk 15 min along the terraces and you are alone.
places.april: End of the flooded season; planting starts in April, so expect a mix of water mirrors and the first green. Fog at dawn is common and beautiful.
places.health: Village level ~1,600–1,900 m. The Red River valley below is hot lowland with more mosquitoes.

places.name: Jianshui Old Town
places.tagline: A lived-in Ming-era town with one of China's largest Confucian temples, and the gateway to Yuanyang.
places.best_for: Architecture, food (grilled tofu!), easy-going town life
description: Jianshui escaped the theme-park treatment of Lijiang: locals still draw water from the old wells. Highlights are the vast **Confucius Temple**, the labyrinthine **Zhu Family Garden**, the 17-arch **Double Dragon Bridge** and the village of **Tuanshan** (by the little heritage railway).
Grilled tofu (烧豆腐) at night on every corner.
places.april: Warm and dry, ~26 °C days.

places.name: Xishuangbanna Tropical Botanical Garden
places.name_zh: 中科院西双版纳热带植物园
places.tagline: 13,000 plant species on a river island in China's rainforest corner: science-y, lush, and quiet.
places.access: From Jinghong (Xishuangbanna station on the Kunming–Vientiane railway) ~1.5 h by bus.
places.best_for: Rainforest, birds, night walks; Osa-peninsula vibes
description: Run by the Chinese Academy of Sciences, with a research-station hotel inside the garden. Night tours, a primary-rainforest trail and the Dai culture of Xishuangbanna around it.
Xishuangbanna is China's tropical south-east Asia: Dai temples, tea mountains (Pu'er!) and the train continues to Laos.
places.april: Hot (30–35 °C) and dry, before the monsoon. Mid-April brings the Dai **Water-Splashing Festival**: big fun, big crowds in Jinghong.
places.health: **Inside the southern Yunnan mosquito zone** (dengue, chikungunya; *Aedes aegypti* present). See the health layer; if pregnant, consider skipping or use strict bite protection.

photos.credit: No machine-readable author provided. Calips assumed (based on copyright claims).

places.name: Longji (Dragon's Backbone) Terraces
places.tagline: Zhuang and Yao villages perched on terraced ridges; hike from Dazhai to Ping'an.
places.access: HSR to Guilin North, then bus/driver (~2 h). Also reachable from Sanjiang South HSR.
places.best_for: Village-to-village hiking, Yao culture
description: Two terrace areas: **Ping'an** (Zhuang, busier, accessible) and **Dazhai/Jinkeng** (Red Yao, bigger and more dramatic, cable car to viewpoints). The 4–5 h trail between Dazhai, Tiantouzhai and Ping'an is the best way to see them.
Long-haired Red Yao women of Huangluo village are a (touristy) highlight.
places.crowd_tips: Stay overnight up in the villages; day-trippers leave by 16:00.
places.april: Terraces being flooded and planted (late April–May): water reflections, misty. Some rain.

places.name: Zhaoxing Dong Village
places.tagline: Five drum towers and wind-and-rain bridges in one of the largest Dong villages, now minutes from an HSR station.
places.access: HSR Guiyang/Guilin → Congjiang (Guiyang–Guangzhou line), then ~30 min by taxi/bus.
places.best_for: Dong culture, polyphonic singing, rice-field walks
description: Zhaoxing itself has become quite commercial, but the surrounding hills are full of smaller Dong villages (**Tang'an**, **Jitang**, **Xiage**) linked by footpaths through rice terraces. Dong 'grand songs' (UNESCO-listed polyphonic singing) are performed in the evenings.
A good 'step' between Guangxi and Yunnan on the south-western HSR network.
places.crowd_tips: Walk up to Tang'an (1.5 h) for a much quieter village.
places.april: Spring green, rice planting, ~20 °C, rain likely.

places.name: Huaqiangbei Electronics Markets
places.tagline: The world's hardware bazaar: floor after floor of chips, drones, phone parts and prototype gadgets.
places.access: From Hong Kong via Futian/Lok Ma Chau checkpoint, then Shenzhen Metro to Huaqiang Rd (~1 h door to door).
places.best_for: Tech nerds; seeing Shenzhen's maker culture
description: Start in **SEG Electronics Market** (components on the lower floors, drones and gadgets higher up) and **Huaqiang Electronics World**. It's wholesale-first, but stalls happily sell single items.
Pair with the Shenzhen skyline (Ping An Finance Centre), the OCT Loft art district, or a hike on Wutong Shan.
places.crowd_tips: Weekday mornings are calmer; many stalls close by ~18:00.
places.april: Warm and humid (~27 °C), first heavy showers.

places.name: Sai Kung East: Tai Long Wan & High Island
places.name_zh: 西貢東郊野公園 · 大浪灣
places.tagline: Hong Kong's wild side: volcanic hexagonal columns, empty surf beaches and a ridge hike on MacLehose Stage 2.
places.access: MTR to Diamond Hill / Hang Hau, then bus/minibus to Sai Kung and taxi to East Dam / Sai Wan Pavilion.
places.best_for: Coastal hiking, swimming, geology
description: Start at the **East Dam of High Island Reservoir** (UNESCO Global Geopark: giant hexagonal rock columns), then hike MacLehose Stage 2 via **Sai Wan, Ham Tin and Tai Wan**, three of the best beaches in Hong Kong, with seafood shacks. Finish by speedboat from Sai Wan or hike out to Pak Tam Au.
Alternatives nearby: Sharp Peak (steep, exposed scramble), Dragon's Back on HK Island (easier, much busier).
places.crowd_tips: Weekdays are wonderfully empty. Weekends and public holidays get busy.
places.april: ~24 °C, humid, hazy days possible; sea still cool for swimming.

places.name: Wulong Karst: Three Natural Bridges
places.tagline: Gigantic limestone bridges and sinkholes, 2 hours from Chongqing. A UNESCO karst landscape.
places.access: Train or bus Chongqing → Wulong (~1.5–2 h), then shuttle buses to the sights.
places.best_for: Jaw-dropping scale; Fairy Mountain grasslands; Furong cave
description: The **Three Natural Bridges** (天生三桥) are collapsed caves forming 200 m-high arches over a gorge, and they're truly epic. **Longshuixia Fissure** is a narrow slot canyon. **Fairy Mountain (Xiannüshan)** is a high plateau of meadows and forest.
The infrastructure is very Chinese-mass-tourism (lifts, shuttle buses, crowds at the viewpoints), but the scenery wins.
places.crowd_tips: Go on a weekday, arrive at opening; stay overnight in Xiannüshan town to be first in line.
places.april: Green and mild (~20 °C), misty; Fairy Mountain much cooler.
places.health: Fairy Mountain tops out ~2,000 m, below the 2,500 m threshold.

places.name: Chongqing: Hongyadong & the vertical city
places.tagline: China's most cinematic megacity: stilt houses, monorails through buildings, cliffs, bridges and hotpot fog.
places.access: HSR Chengdu → Chongqing (1–1.5 h). Metro + walking; everything is up or down stairs.
places.best_for: City-explorers who loved Tokyo
description: **Hongyadong** (a lit-up stilt-house complex on the Jialing cliff) is the Instagram icon. It's a madhouse at night, so **look at it from the Qiansimen Bridge or the opposite bank instead**.

Then explore the vertical old town: the **Shibati** stairway neighbourhood, the **Yangtze River Cableway**, **Liziba** (where the monorail drives *through* an apartment block), **Eling Park** and the **Kuixinglou** 'ground floor on the 22nd floor'. Eat hotpot, xiaomian noodles and street skewers.
places.crowd_tips: Hongyadong at 17:00–22:00 is peak chaos. Go at 7–9 am for empty walkways, or skip it and walk Shibati at dusk.
places.april: ~22 °C / 15 °C, often grey and humid; less smog than winter.

places.name: Hong Kong's wild east: Sai Kung & Plover Cove
places.tagline: Two-thirds of Hong Kong is countryside, and this is its wildest corner: volcanic coast, empty Hakka villages, sea kayaks and kaito ferries.
places.nearest_station: Hong Kong West Kowloon (HSR) → MTR to Diamond Hill / Hang Hau / University
places.best_for: Coastal hikes, beaches, kayaking, abandoned-village atmosphere
description: The Sai Kung peninsula and the Plover Cove / Double Haven country parks are a maze of geopark coastline, islands and walled Hakka villages abandoned in the 1960s–70s. Some, like **Lai Chi Wo**, are being revived with farm-stays and cafés.
On a weekday it's hard to believe you are 30 km from Central.
highlights: MacLehose Stage 2 & the Tai Long Wan beaches
High Island East Dam hexagonal columns
Kaito ferry from Ma Liu Shui to Tap Mun / Lai Chi Wo (weekends)
Sea-kayaking among the geopark sea caves
places.getting_around: MTR + green minibuses and buses from Sai Kung town; taxis to trailheads; weekend kaito ferries to the northern villages. No car needed.
places.stay: Few beds out here: Sai Kung town (seafood waterfront), a campsite at Ham Tin, or the Lai Chi Wo village homestays. Most people base in Kowloon.
places.route_idea: Day 1: East Dam → MacLehose 2 → speedboat from Sai Wan. Day 2 (weekend): ferry to Lai Chi Wo, walk the Plover Cove trail.
places.april: ~24 °C, humid, first heavy showers; sea still fresh.

places.name: South Lantau & Tai O
places.tagline: Hong Kong's biggest island: a 934 m peak, buffalo on the beaches, a giant Buddha and a stilt-house fishing village.
places.best_for: Sunrise hike, beach villages, Tai O stilt houses
description: Ngong Ping with the Big Buddha is mobbed; the rest of South Lantau is mellow beach villages (Pui O, Cheung Sha, Mui Wo) and steep trails. **Lantau Peak** (934 m) for sunrise is one of Hong Kong's great hikes.
**Tai O**, a Tanka fishing village on stilts, is at its best early or late when the tour buses have gone.
highlights: Tai O stilt houses & salted-fish stalls
Water buffalo on Pui O beach
Ferry back from Mui Wo to Central
places.getting_around: Buses from Tung Chung / Mui Wo cover the whole south coast; ferries from Central to Mui Wo.
places.stay: Tai O Heritage Hotel (former police station), beach guesthouses in Pui O / Cheung Sha, or Mui Wo.
places.april: Clear mornings possible, often hazy; good hiking temperatures.

places.name: Dapeng Peninsula (Shenzhen)
places.tagline: Shenzhen's green end: a coastal scramble, the city's best beaches, a Ming-dynasty fort and its highest mountain.
places.nearest_station: Shenzhen North / Futian (HSR), then bus or Didi ~1.5 h
places.best_for: Seeing how Shenzhen relaxes; coastal hiking
description: A UNESCO-geopark peninsula east of the megacity. **Qiniangshan** (869 m) gives views over Hong Kong's Mirs Bay. The **Dongchong–Xichong coastal trek** (~8 km, rock-hopping) is a classic, and **Dapeng Fortress** is a 600-year-old walled town that still feels lived-in.
Weekends turn Xichong beach and Jiaochangwei into a party; weekdays are calm.
places.getting_around: Buses from Shenzhen metro terminals or Didi (~¥150 from Futian). Local buses link the beaches.
places.stay: Jiaochangwei (较场尾) has dozens of boutique B&Bs; Xichong guesthouses.
places.april: Warm, humid, ~25 °C; beaches quiet before the summer season.

places.name: Li River & Yulong valley karst
places.tagline: The karst towers on the 20-yuan note. Famous for good reason, and the side valleys are still pastoral if you cycle away from Yangshuo.
places.best_for: Cycling, bamboo rafting, climbing, karst hikes
description: **Yangshuo** town (West Street) is a backpacker-party magnet. The magic lies in the countryside: e-bike or cycle the **Yulong River valley** between Jiuxian, Chaolong and Jima past rice paddies and karst towers. Walk the riverside path from **Yangdi to Xingping** (~4 h), the best stretch of the Li River.
Xingping's **Laozhai Hill** (300+ steps) gives the iconic sunrise view.
places.getting_around: Rent bicycles or e-bikes in Yangshuo/Xingping; bamboo rafts on the Yulong; local buses and Didi. HSR Yangshuo station is ~30 min from town.
places.stay: Farmhouse guesthouses along the Yulong river (Jiuxian, Chaolong) or old Xingping; avoid West Street.
places.route_idea: Guilin North HSR → Daxu old town → raft/walk Yangdi–Xingping → 2 nights in a Yulong farmhouse → Yangshuo HSR onward.
places.crowd_tips: The main Li River cruise and West Street are rammed; side valleys at 8 am are blissful.
places.april: Rainy season begins: misty, very green, rivers fuller; 18–25 °C.

places.name: Longsheng & Sanjiang: terraces and Dong bridges
places.tagline: Zhuang and Yao terraces in the east, Dong drum towers and the Chengyang wind-and-rain bridge in the west, linked by mountain roads.
places.best_for: Terrace hiking, minority villages, timber architecture
description: Longsheng's **Longji terraces** (Ping'an, Dazhai, Tiantouzhai) climb entire mountains. West towards Sanjiang the culture switches to the **Dong**, master carpenters whose covered bridges and drum towers are built without nails. **Chengyang** has eight villages strung along a river with the most famous bridge (1912).
places.getting_around: HSR to Sanjiang South for the Dong side; buses or a hired car to Longji (~1.5 h). A driver for a day connects both.
places.stay: Terrace-top guesthouses in Dazhai/Tiantouzhai (porters carry luggage); Chengyang village inns.
places.april: Terraces being flooded and planted; rain likely; ~20 °C.

places.name: Southeast Guizhou: Miao & Dong heartland
places.tagline: China's most intact minority heartland: hundreds of Miao and Dong villages, wooden stilt houses, rice terraces, festivals, silver and batik.
places.nearest_station: Kaili South (Shanghai–Kunming HSR) in the north; Rongjiang & Congjiang (Guiyang–Guangzhou HSR) in the south
places.best_for: Road-tripping between villages, festivals, crafts, homestays, our 'authentic' core
description: Qiandongnan prefecture is the region to roam. The **Miao** north (Leishan, Taijiang, Shidong) and the **Dong** south (Rongjiang, Congjiang, Liping, Zhaoxing) are linked by winding roads through terraced valleys. Some villages are tourist showcases (Xijiang, Zhaoxing), but many more (Langde, Tang'an, Basha's hamlets, Jitang, the Leishan villages) are simply villages.
Market days rotate between towns on a fixed cycle (赶场 gǎnchǎng): ask locally which village has a market tomorrow.
highlights: **Sisters' Meal Festival** (Miao), Shidong/Taijiang, 15th–17th day of the 3rd lunar month = **21–23 April 2027**
Langde Upper Village and the old Miao paths around Leishan
Dong grand song in Xiaohuang or Zhaoxing
Zhenyuan old town in its gorge (north edge)
Basha, the Miao 'gunmen' village near Congjiang
places.getting_around: Two HSR lines frame the region: **Kaili South** in the north (Shanghai–Kunming line) and **Rongjiang / Congjiang** in the south (Guiyang–Guangzhou line). In between, local buses are slow but cheap; the best option is **a car with driver for 3–5 days**, or self-drive with a Chinese temporary permit.
places.stay: Family guesthouses in Langde, Xijiang (book a hillside room), Tang'an, Zhaoxing; boutique stays around Leishan and Zhenyuan.
places.route_idea: Kaili → Shidong (festival) → Langde & Xijiang → Leishan → Rongjiang → Basha & Congjiang → Tang'an & Zhaoxing → HSR Congjiang onward to Guilin or Guiyang (5–6 days).
places.april: Planting season, green, mild (18–24 °C), rain showers. The Sisters' Meal Festival falls right in your window.

places.name: Libo & Maolan karst forests
places.tagline: UNESCO South China Karst: turquoise pools, waterfalls and the world's largest karst primary forest.
places.best_for: Waterfalls and forest walks; a calmer alternative to Jiuzhaigou-style scenery
description: **Xiaoqikong** is the showpiece: a series of jade pools, cascades and a seven-arch bridge, beautiful but busy. **Dakikong** and especially the **Maolan** reserve (karst cone forest with Yao and Shui villages) are quieter and wilder.
places.getting_around: HSR to Libo; shuttle buses to Xiaoqikong; a car/driver for Maolan.
places.stay: Libo town or guesthouses near Xiaoqikong's gate.
places.april: Water levels rising, lush; mild and showery.

places.name: Western Hunan (Xiangxi): Fenghuang, Dehang & Furong
places.tagline: Miao and Tujia country: riverside stilt-house towns, canyons and one of the world's most spectacular suspension bridges.
places.best_for: Old towns at dusk, canyon hikes, Miao culture
description: **Fenghuang** is gorgeous and heaving: stilt houses on the Tuo River, lantern-lit nights, bars. **Dehang** Miao village sits in a canyon with waterfall hikes, beneath the **Aizhai Bridge** (1,176 m span, 330 m high). **Furong town** is a waterfall-front Tujia village.
This is a natural stop if you travel Zhangjiajie → Guizhou.
highlights: Fenghuang at blue hour and early morning
places.getting_around: HSR (Zhangjiajie–Jishou–Fenghuang–Huaihua) plus buses; Dehang 30 min from Jishou.
places.stay: Fenghuang riverside inns (pick the quieter north bank), Dehang village guesthouses.
places.crowd_tips: Fenghuang's evening is shoulder-to-shoulder; get up at 6:30 for misty, empty lanes.
places.april: Spring rain, misty rivers, 15–22 °C.

places.name: Zhangjiajie & Wulingyuan
places.tagline: 3,000 sandstone pillars in the clouds (the 'Avatar mountains'): one of Earth's most surreal landscapes, and China's crowd magnets.
places.best_for: Jaw-dropping scenery if you can handle crowds
description: Wulingyuan (UNESCO) contains Zhangjiajie National Forest Park, Tianzi Shan, Yuanjiajie and Yangjiajie. Shuttle buses, elevators and cable cars move huge numbers of people between viewpoints.
**Tips**: walk the **Golden Whip Stream** early, do **Yangjiajie** (less visited, a ridge scramble) and stay *inside* or at a back gate to be on the platforms before the tours arrive.
places.getting_around: Park shuttle buses (included in the multi-day ticket). HSR to Zhangjiajie West then bus to Wulingyuan town.
places.stay: Wulingyuan town (east gate) or the guesthouses near Tianzi Shan / Yangjiajie.
places.crowd_tips: Weekdays only; queue for the Bailong elevator early or skip it. Avoid 1–5 May at all costs.
places.april: Often misty, which is atmospheric but views come and go; 15–22 °C.

places.name: Honghe: Jianshui to the Hani terraces
places.tagline: From a Confucian old town across the Red River gorge into mountains sculpted by Hani rice terraces.
places.best_for: Road trip, village homestays, photography
description: Two very different worlds 2.5 hours apart: **Jianshui** (Ming-era town, Confucius temple, grilled tofu) and the **Yuanyang terraces**, where Hani and Yi villages sit among water-filled terraces.
Between them the road drops into the hot **Red River valley** and climbs again, a great drive.
places.getting_around: Fast rail Kunming → Jianshui; then bus or driver to Xinjie/Yuanyang. Terrace viewpoints are spread out, so hire a driver locally (~¥300–500/day) or self-drive.
places.stay: Courtyard hotels in Jianshui; homestays in Azheke, Pugaolao or Duoyishu.
places.april: End of the water season and start of planting; dry, sunny, foggy dawns.

places.name: Erhai Lake & Cangshan
places.tagline: A high lake ringed by Bai villages, under a 4,000 m mountain wall. Dali's old town is busy; the villages and trails are not.
places.best_for: Cycling the lake, Bai architecture, hiking the Cangshan 'Jade Belt'
description: Dali old town is a lively (crowded) hub. Head north to **Xizhou**, a beautiful Bai merchant town with courtyard mansions and *baba* flatbread, then up the lake to **Shuanglang** and around the quieter east shore.
The **Cangshan Jade Belt Road** is an 18 km contour path at ~2,600 m above the lake (cable cars up), with temples like **Jizhao'an** below.
places.getting_around: E-bikes and bicycles around the lake; Didi everywhere; HSR Dali station.
places.stay: Xizhou courtyard guesthouses (calmer than Dali old town), Shuanglang lakeside (pretty but touristy).
places.april: Dry, sunny, windy afternoons; 22 °C / 10 °C.
places.health: The lake is at ~1,970 m. The Jade Belt Road is ~2,600 m, fine as a day hike; you sleep lower.

places.name: Tea Horse Road highlands: Shaxi, Jianchuan & Nuodeng
places.name_zh: 茶马古道 · 沙溪—诺邓
places.tagline: Old caravan towns in quiet valleys: Shaxi's market square, Jianchuan's woodcarvers and Nuodeng's 1,000-year-old salt village.
places.best_for: Slow travel, back roads, nights in old caravan inns
description: West of the Dali–Lijiang tourist corridor lies a different Yunnan: the **Shaxi valley** with its restored Sideng market square; **Shibaoshan**, with Nanzhao-era grottoes on a forested ridge; **Jianchuan**, home of Bai woodcarving; and, 3 hours of mountain road further south-west, **Nuodeng**, a terraced salt-well village famous for its cured ham.
Foreign visitors are rare beyond Shaxi.
places.getting_around: **Car essential** (or driver). Jianchuan station → Shaxi 45 min; Shaxi → Nuodeng ~3 h via Yunlong.
places.stay: Shaxi guesthouses (many lovely ones), Nuodeng village inns.
places.april: Dry season, sunny days ~22 °C, cool nights.

places.name: Lijiang, Jade Dragon & Tiger Leaping Gorge
places.name_zh: 丽江 · 玉龙雪山 · 虎跳峡
places.tagline: Naxi villages under a 5,596 m glacier peak, the first bend of the Yangtze, and the great gorge walk.
places.best_for: Mountain scenery with comfortable bases; the Haba–Baishuitai back road
description: **Lijiang old town** is pretty but a theme park; stay outside it. **Baisha** and **Yuhu** villages sit right under Jade Dragon Snow Mountain. **Shigu** marks the first bend of the Yangtze, and **Tiger Leaping Gorge** cuts between Jade Dragon and **Haba** (5,396 m).
Beyond the gorge a quiet road climbs past Haba village to **Baishuitai**, white travertine terraces in a Naxi heartland.
places.getting_around: Fast rail to Lijiang; Didi, drivers and buses; the Haba/Baishuitai road needs a car.
places.stay: Baisha/Yuhu Naxi courtyard guesthouses, Shuhe (quieter than the old town), TLG guesthouses.
places.april: Dry, sunny, strong UV; ~20 °C days, near-freezing nights.
places.health: **Lijiang itself is ~2,400 m, right at the threshold.** Haba village is ~2,700 m, Baishuitai ~2,400 m, and the Jade Dragon glacier cable car goes to 4,500 m+, so skip it if pregnant. TLG guesthouses are ~2,000–2,300 m.

places.name: Shangri-La plateau & Meili (Diqing)
places.tagline: Tibetan Yunnan: monasteries, yak pastures, the Jinsha canyon at Benzilan and the sacred Meili range.
places.best_for: Tibetan culture, big mountain trekking
description: **Shangri-La** (Gyalthang) with its rebuilt old town and the great **Songzanlin monastery** sits on a 3,300 m plateau. The road north drops into the arid Jinsha canyon at **Benzilan**, then climbs over passes to **Deqin** and **Feilaisi** facing Kawagebo.
Yubeng village is reached only on foot or by mule.
places.getting_around: Train to Shangri-La; buses/driver beyond (Shangri-La → Deqin 4–5 h).
places.stay: Shangri-La old town guesthouses; Feilaisi lodges with mountain view; Yubeng guesthouses.
places.april: Clear, cold (night frost), rhododendrons starting; occasional snow on passes.
places.health: **Almost all overnight stops are above 3,000 m** (Shangri-La 3,300 m, Deqin 3,400 m). Not advisable in pregnancy; otherwise acclimatise and ascend gradually.

places.name: Nujiang Valley: Grand Canyon of the Salween
places.tagline: A 300 km gorge between 4,000 m ranges, home to Lisu, Nu and Dulong people and Tibetan-Catholic villages. Yunnan at its most remote.
places.nearest_station: Baoshan or Dali (fast rail), then 3–4 h by road to Liuku
places.best_for: An adventure road trip far off the tourist map
description: The Nu (Salween) river runs parallel to the Mekong and Yangtze in the 'Three Parallel Rivers' UNESCO area. A single road follows it north from **Liuku** past cliffside Lisu villages, the 'Stone Moon' arch near **Fugong**, **Laomudeng** (a Nu village with a church and views), to **Bingzhongluo**, where Tibetan, Nu and Lisu cultures and Catholic churches mix at the river's 'first bend'.
Few foreigners, simple but friendly guesthouses, a real expedition feel.
places.getting_around: Buses up the valley, or a driver from Liuku/Dali. The road is long and winding, so allow time. April is dry season (fewer landslides).
places.stay: Guesthouses in Liuku, Laomudeng, Gongshan and Bingzhongluo.
places.april: Dry, warm in the valley (~25 °C), peach blossom lingering up north.
places.health: Valley floor 800–1,800 m. Side trips (e.g. Dulong tunnel road) go higher; remote, so medical care is hours away.

places.name: Tengchong: volcanoes, hot springs & Heshun
places.tagline: A green volcanic basin near Myanmar: hot springs, wetlands, jade traders and Heshun, a well-off overseas-Chinese home town.
places.nearest_station: Baoshan (fast rail) + 2 h road, or fly to Tengchong
places.best_for: Relaxed cycling, hot springs, a 'different' Yunnan
description: **Heshun** is a remarkably pretty, prosperous village of grey-tiled houses, ancestral halls and a famous library, built with money sent home by emigrants to Burma. Around it are extinct volcano cones, the **Rehai** hot springs and **Beihai** floating-grass wetland.
places.getting_around: Didi and buses around Tengchong; bicycles in Heshun.
places.stay: Courtyard guesthouses in Heshun.
places.april: Spring, dry, ~24 °C.

places.name: Xishuangbanna: Dai villages, rainforest & tea mountains
places.tagline: China's tropical south-east Asia: Dai temples, rainforest, wild elephants and the Pu'er tea mountains, at the end of the train to Laos.
places.best_for: Tropical nature, tea culture, Dai Buddhism
description: **Jinghong** is the hub. Around it lie Dai villages with Theravada temples (**Ganlanba/Menghan**), the **Botanical Garden** at Menglun, and in the west the cool **tea mountains** of Menghai (Nannuo, Bulang, Laobanzhang) with Hani and Bulang villages among ancient tea trees.
places.getting_around: Fast rail Kunming → Jinghong (3.5 h); buses/driver to the tea mountains.
places.stay: Jinghong riverside hotels, tea-farm guesthouses in Menghai, XTBG's research hotel.
places.april: **Hottest and driest** month (30–35 °C). The **Water-Splashing Festival on 13–15 April** is great fun but brings huge crowds and price spikes.
places.health: **Mosquito zone** (dengue, chikungunya; *Aedes aegypti* present). The tea mountains (1,200–1,800 m) carry much lower risk than Jinghong and the lowlands. If pregnant, think twice.

places.name: Jingmai Mountain ancient tea forests
places.tagline: UNESCO World Heritage (2023): a thousand-year-old tea landscape with Blang and Dai villages under ancient trees.
places.nearest_station: Pu'er (fast rail) + ~3.5 h, or from Menghai ~2 h
places.best_for: Tea culture, village walks, cool mountain nights
description: Unlike plantations, the tea here grows under the forest canopy, a centuries-old agro-forestry system. **Wengji** and **Nuogang** villages keep traditional stilt houses; you can pick and roast tea with families.
places.getting_around: Car or driver from Menghai/Lancang.
places.stay: Family tea guesthouses in Jingmai/Mangjing villages.
places.april: **Spring tea harvest**, the best month to visit. Dry and warm.
places.health: Mountain elevation (~1,500 m) and much lower mosquito risk than the lowlands, but it is inside the southern-Yunnan health zone.

places.name: Puzhehei karst lakes
places.tagline: Karst hills reflected in lily-pad lakes, with Yi villages to cycle between. A handy stop on the HSR from Guangxi to Kunming.
places.best_for: Easy cycling and boating, a rest day between big cities
description: A smaller, quieter cousin of Guilin's karst on a high plateau. Rent a bike, paddle a boat and climb **Qinglong Shan** for the view over the lakes.
places.getting_around: Bicycles and e-bikes; the HSR station is ~15 min away.
places.stay: Lakeside village guesthouses (Xianrendong village).
places.april: Dry spring; lotus season is later (June–August).

places.name: Jiarong Tibetan valleys: Siguniang & Danba
places.name_zh: 嘉绒藏区 · 四姑娘山—丹巴
places.tagline: A road trip from panda country over the Balang pass into Tibetan valleys of stone towers and painted villages.
places.best_for: Road trip, Tibetan villages, mountain hikes
description: From Wolong the road climbs to the **Balang Shan** tunnel (~3,850 m) and drops to **Rilong**, base for Siguniang's valleys. It then follows the river down through **Xiaojin** to **Danba**, a deep valley at only ~1,900 m famous for **Jiaju** (painted Jiarong Tibetan houses on a sunny slope) and the ancient stone watchtowers of **Suopo** and **Zhonglu**.
**Pregnancy-friendly trick:** you can see real Tibetan village life while sleeping at ~2,000 m in Danba/Jiaju instead of 3,200 m in Rilong.
places.getting_around: Car/driver (most practical), or buses Chengdu → Rilong → Danba. Chengdu → Danba ~6–7 h.
places.stay: Jiaju or Zhonglu family homestays; Rilong lodges for Siguniang.
places.route_idea: Chengdu → Wolong (pandas, night) → Balang pass → Rilong (only if altitude OK) → Xiaojin → Danba/Jiaju 2 nights → back via Kangding or the same road.
places.april: Pear and apricot blossom in Danba's valleys (late March–April); snow on the passes.
places.health: Rilong 3,200 m and the Balang tunnel ~3,850 m are high. Danba/Jiaju (~1,900–2,200 m) are fine for overnights.

places.name: Ya'an cloud forests: Bifengxia, Labahe & Erlangshan
places.name_zh: 雅安 · 碧峰峡 · 喇叭河
places.tagline: The 'rain city': misty gorges, the birthplace of cultivated tea, a panda base and red-panda forests, 1 hour from Chengdu.
places.best_for: Lush, quiet nature near Chengdu; pandas without crowds
description: **Bifengxia** has a gorge walk and a panda base. **Mengdingshan** is where tea was first cultivated (legend says 2,000 years ago). **Shangli** is a riverside old town. **Labahe** in Tianquan is cloud forest with hot springs and red pandas, part of the Giant Panda National Park.
places.getting_around: Fast rail to Ya'an; buses and Didi; car for Labahe.
places.stay: Shangli guesthouses, Labahe lodges.
places.april: Rainy and green (it rains here more than anywhere in Sichuan); ~18 °C.

places.name: Qingchengshan & Dujiangyan
places.tagline: A Taoist mountain and a 2,200-year-old irrigation system that still works, 40 minutes from Chengdu by HSR.
places.best_for: An easy escape from Chengdu with forest trails
description: **Qingchengshan** is one of the cradles of Taoism. The 'front mountain' has temples and crowds, while the **back mountain (Houshan)** has gorge trails and village guesthouses. **Dujiangyan** (UNESCO) is the ingenious 256 BC water system that made the Chengdu plain fertile. Nearby **Jiezi** is a riverside old town.
places.getting_around: HSR from Chengdu; buses between the sites.
places.stay: Back-mountain guesthouses at Tai'an old town.
places.april: Green and pleasant, ~20 °C; misty.

places.name: Songpan, Huanglong & Jiuzhaigou
places.name_zh: 九寨沟 · 黄龙 · 松潘
places.tagline: The famous turquoise lakes of Jiuzhaigou and the travertine pools of Huanglong, now reachable by train from Chengdu.
places.best_for: Postcard scenery, if you accept crowds and altitude
description: **Jiuzhaigou**'s lakes are genuinely unreal in colour; the park is very well run and very busy. **Huanglong** is a 3,100–3,600 m valley of yellow travertine terraces. **Songpan** is an old walled garrison town with horse-trekking outfits.
Since the new railway, Chengdu → Huanglong Jiuzhai takes a few hours instead of a 10-hour bus ride (check the current timetable).
places.getting_around: HSR to Huanglong Jiuzhai, then shuttle buses; park buses inside Jiuzhaigou.
places.stay: Jiuzhaigou gate area hotels/Tibetan guesthouses; Songpan old town.
places.crowd_tips: Enter at opening, take the bus to the top and walk down; weekdays.
places.april: Lakes thawed but trees still bare; snow possible. The scenery peaks in October.
places.health: **Overnights 2,000–3,000 m; Huanglong reaches 3,600 m.** Discuss with your doctor if pregnant.

places.name: Wulong karst & Fairy Mountain
places.tagline: Natural bridges, sinkholes and slot canyons below a cool alpine meadow plateau, 2 hours from Chongqing.
places.best_for: Karst wonders plus quiet villages on the plateau
description: The famous sights (Three Natural Bridges, Longshuixia fissure, Furong Cave) are on tour-bus circuits. **Fairy Mountain (Xiannüshan)** plateau has meadows, forests and villages where Chongqing locals escape the heat; **Houping** further north has giant tiankeng sinkholes and few visitors.
places.getting_around: Train/bus to Wulong; shuttle buses to sights; a car for Houping.
places.stay: Xiannüshan town hotels (cool, convenient for early starts).
places.april: Fresh green, ~20 °C below, ~12 °C on the plateau.

places.name: Wujiang gorges & Tujia towns (SE Chongqing)
places.name_zh: 乌江 · 龚滩 · 濯水
places.tagline: Cliffside river towns, Tujia stilt houses and emerald gorges in Chongqing's forgotten south-east corner.
places.nearest_station: Pengshui West, Qianjiang (HSR from Chongqing ~1–1.5 h); Youyang
places.best_for: An off-track loop before/after Chongqing; river towns
description: The **Wujiang** (Wu River) cuts a deep green gorge to the Yangtze. Along it: **Gongtan**, a Tujia stilt-house town rebuilt on the cliffs above the river; **Ayi River** canyon near Pengshui (Miao); **Zhuoshui** old town with one of China's longest wind-and-rain bridges; **Youyang's Taohuayuan** ('Peach Blossom Spring') karst valley.
Mainly domestic visitors and very few foreigners.
places.getting_around: HSR Chongqing → Pengshui West / Qianjiang, then buses or a driver; the river road Pengshui → Gongtan is beautiful.
places.stay: Gongtan riverside guesthouses, Zhuoshui inns.
places.april: Mild, green, some rain; ~22 °C.

places.name: Yangtze Three Gorges: Fengjie & Wushan
places.name_zh: 长江三峡 · 奉节—巫山
places.tagline: Qutang and Wu gorges, the Kuimen gate on the 10-yuan note, and boat trips up the Little Three Gorges, now reachable by HSR.
places.best_for: A classic China landscape without a 4-day cruise
description: You don't need a cruise any more: the HSR stops at **Fengjie** and **Wushan**. From Fengjie visit **Baidicheng** temple and the **Kuimen** gate of Qutang Gorge; from Wushan take boats into the **Little Three Gorges** of the Daning River and hike above the **Wu Gorge** to Goddess Peak.
The dam raised the water by ~100 m, so the gorges are less wild than in old photos but still grand.
highlights: Goddess Peak trail above Wu Gorge
Wushan's red autumn leaves (not in April)
places.getting_around: HSR from Chongqing North (~2 h); taxis and tour boats locally.
places.stay: Wushan or Fengjie riverside hotels.
places.april: Spring, mild, often misty in the gorges.

places.name: Leshan Giant Buddha
places.tagline: A 71 m Buddha carved into a river cliff in the 8th century, the largest stone Buddha in the world.
places.access: HSR to Leshan, bus/taxi 20 min. Combine with Mount Emei.
description: Staggering in scale. The staircase down beside the Buddha queues for hours on busy days, so consider seeing it **from a boat** (20 min, no queue) and walking the quieter cliff temples (Wuyou Temple) instead.
places.crowd_tips: Arrive at opening (7:30) on a weekday or take the boat.

places.name: Xijiang Thousand-Household Miao Village
places.tagline: The world's largest Miao village: 1,000+ wooden houses on two hillsides. Spectacular at night, very touristy by day.
description: Xijiang has become a stage set with a main street of shops, but the scale of the stilt-house village lit up at night is unforgettable. Stay up the hill and walk the back lanes and rice fields early in the morning.
places.crowd_tips: Day-trippers leave by 17:00; mornings are lovely.

places.name: Langde Upper Village
places.tagline: A small, authentic Miao village with cobbled lanes and a dance ground, linked to Xijiang by old footpaths.
description: Langde is what Xijiang was 20 years ago: a protected, still-farming Miao village on a river bend. Villagers perform welcoming dances for groups. There's a beautiful 4–5 h walk on old paths over the ridge to Xijiang.

places.name: Basha Miao Village
places.tagline: The last 'gunmen' tribe: Miao men who carry muskets and wear topknots, in hamlets among sacred forest.
description: Basha's five hamlets above Congjiang worship trees and keep a distinctive culture. Performances for visitors are touristy, but walking the forest paths between the hamlets is not.

places.name: Tang'an Dong Village
places.tagline: A Dong 'eco-museum' village perched above terraces, a 1.5 h walk up from Zhaoxing.
description: Spectacular terraced setting with a drum tower and wooden houses; one of the first eco-museums in China (with Norwegian help). Far quieter than Zhaoxing below.

places.name: Chengyang Wind-and-Rain Bridge
places.tagline: The finest of the Dong covered bridges (1912), built without a single nail, with eight villages along the river.
description: Walk across, then explore the eight villages (Ma'an, Pingzhai, Yanzhai…) with drum towers, water wheels and tea fields. Stay the night for evening Dong songs.

places.name: Xiaoqikong (Libo)
places.tagline: Turquoise karst pools, cascades and a Qing-dynasty seven-arch bridge in forest.
description: A well-built boardwalk circuit through a forested karst valley: the 68-level falls, Wolong pools, Water Forest (walk through ankle-deep water). Very popular on weekends.
places.crowd_tips: Weekdays, early entry.

places.name: Fenghuang Ancient Town
places.tagline: Stilt houses over the Tuo River, the most photogenic old town in China, and among the busiest.
description: Beautiful at dawn and blue hour, noisy at night (bars and karaoke). Stay on the quieter edges and walk the city wall and Hong Bridge at 6:30.
places.crowd_tips: Mornings only; avoid holidays absolutely.

places.name: Dehang Canyon & Aizhai Bridge
places.name_zh: 德夯大峡谷 · 矮寨大桥
places.tagline: A Miao village in a deep canyon with waterfall trails, beneath one of the world's most spectacular suspension bridges.
description: Hike the canyon trails to Liusha waterfall (one of China's tallest, ~216 m), then visit the Aizhai Bridge (1,176 m span) with its glass walkway beneath the deck.

places.name: Zhangjiajie Forest Park
places.tagline: The sandstone pillars of the Avatar films. Unreal scenery, unreal crowds.
description: Walk the Golden Whip Stream in the valley and go up to Yuanjiajie and Tianzi Shan for the pillar views. Yangjiajie is the least crowded section.
places.crowd_tips: Weekday, opening time, walk rather than queue for the elevator.

places.name: Xizhou
places.tagline: Bai merchant town of courtyard mansions among rice fields on Erhai Lake. The nicer base than Dali old town.
description: Grand Bai courtyards (Yan family compound), a morning market, *xizhou baba* flatbreads and cycling through the fields to the lake.

places.name: Nuodeng Salt Village
places.tagline: A 1,000-year-old salt-well village terraced up a valley, famous for its cured ham.
description: Bai houses stacked up the slope, an old Confucian temple at the top, salt wells by the stream. Remote, very few foreigners. Bring your appetite for Nuodeng ham.

places.name: Yuhu & Baisha villages
places.tagline: Stone-walled Naxi villages under Jade Dragon Snow Mountain: the Lijiang area as it used to be.
description: Baisha has Ming-dynasty frescoes and an embroidery institute; Yuhu was the home of the explorer-botanist Joseph Rock and has horse trails up to the lake below the snow peak.
places.health: Yuhu is ~2,700 m, above the threshold; Baisha ~2,450 m.

places.name: Baishuitai & Haba
places.tagline: White travertine terraces, the holy site of the Naxi Dongba religion, on the quiet back road beyond Tiger Leaping Gorge.
description: A smaller, quieter Huanglong. Combine with Haba village (base for Haba Snow Mountain climbs) on the scenic road from the gorge to Shangri-La.
places.health: Around 2,400–2,700 m; Haba village sleeps at ~2,650 m.

places.name: Bingzhongluo
places.tagline: End of the road in the Nujiang gorge: Tibetan, Nu and Lisu villages, Catholic churches and the river's dramatic 'first bend'.
places.nearest_station: none: 8+ h from Dali by road
description: A green basin under snowy ridges at the top of the Nujiang Valley. Walk the old Tea Horse Road path along the river cliffs, visit **Chongding church** and **Wuli** village.

places.name: Laomudeng
places.tagline: A Nu village high above the Nujiang, with a church, tea fields and a view of the Stone Moon range.
description: Simple guesthouses, Sunday hymn singing in the church, and hikes along the ridge to Zhiziluo, a former county seat abandoned in the 1980s.

places.name: Heshun
places.tagline: A graceful overseas-Chinese home village with ancestral halls, lotus ponds and a famous 1920s library.
description: Built with remittances from Burma, Heshun is one of Yunnan's prettiest villages. Stroll the washing pavilions, the library and the residence of the philosopher Ai Siqi.

places.name: Wengji (Jingmai)
places.tagline: A Blang village of stilt houses among ancient tea trees, at the heart of the Jingmai UNESCO site.
description: Sleep in a tea family's house, pick spring tea, and walk through forests where tea trees grow under the canopy.
places.april: Spring tea harvest, the best time to visit.

places.name: Azheke Hani Village
places.tagline: A tiny Hani village of mushroom-roofed houses in the terraces, run as a community tourism project.
description: Instead of being bought out by a tourism company, villagers share the ticket income. Guesthouses in restored houses, terrace walks right from the door.

places.name: Jiaju Tibetan Village (Danba)
places.tagline: Painted Jiarong Tibetan houses scattered across a sunny mountainside: one of China's loveliest villages.
description: Stay with a Tibetan family, walk up through orchards to the top houses, and visit the ancient stone watchtowers of nearby **Suopo** and the plateau village of **Zhonglu**.
places.april: Pear and apricot blossom season.
places.health: Sleeping at ~2,000–2,200 m, below the threshold. The roads in cross higher passes.

places.name: Bifengxia Panda Base
places.tagline: Pandas in green gorge-side enclosures, plus a canyon walk, without the Chengdu crowds.
description: Part of the China Conservation and Research Centre for the Giant Panda. Pairs well with Mengdingshan tea and Shangli old town.

places.name: Huanglong
places.tagline: A golden 'dragon' of travertine pools snaking up a valley below 5,588 m Xuebaoding.
description: Thousands of terraced calcite pools in shades of turquoise. A cable car goes up; walk down.
places.health: **3,100–3,600 m**: altitude sickness is common here even on a day trip.

places.name: Jiuzhaigou Valley
places.tagline: Lakes in colours that look photoshopped, waterfalls and Tibetan villages: the most famous national park in China.
description: Bus to the top of one of the two upper branches and walk down boardwalks past Five-Flower Lake, Pearl Shoal and Nuorilang falls. Daily visitor cap; book tickets ahead.
places.crowd_tips: Be at the gate at opening; avoid holidays.

places.name: Gongtan Ancient Town
places.tagline: A Tujia stilt-house town clinging to the cliffs of the emerald Wujiang.
description: Relocated stone by stone when a dam raised the river, Gongtan still feels authentic: stone-slab lanes, wooden houses on stilts, river views from every guesthouse.

places.name: Baidicheng & Kuimen (Qutang Gorge)
places.tagline: A temple on a former hilltop island at the entrance to the Three Gorges, facing the cliffs on the 10-yuan note.
description: Baidicheng (White Emperor City) is steeped in Three Kingdoms legend and Li Bai's poetry. The view into Qutang Gorge through the Kuimen gate is the classic image of the Yangtze.

places.name: Jinfoshan
places.tagline: A cliff-ringed karst table mountain with cave temples, ancient forest and rare golden-hair monkeys nearby.
description: Part of the South China Karst UNESCO site. Cable car up the 300 m cliffs; walk the cliff-top path and the Golden Buddha cave.

places.name: Qingcheng Back Mountain
places.tagline: Gorge trails, waterfalls and village guesthouses on the quiet side of the Taoist mountain.
description: Walk the Feiquan gorge and the trail up to Baiyun temple; stay in Tai'an old town at the trailhead.

places.name: Fanjingshan
places.tagline: A sacred Buddhist mountain whose 'Mushroom Rock' and twin-temple pinnacle (Red Clouds Golden Summit) rise from cloud forest.
places.nearest_station: Tongren or Tongren South (HSR) + 1–1.5 h by road
description: UNESCO natural site and home of the endemic Guizhou snub-nosed monkey. Cable car to ~2,200 m, then steep steps (chains!) up the Golden Summit pinnacle. Stay at **Yunshe** or **Zhaisha** villages at the foot.
places.crowd_tips: Daily visitor caps; book tickets; weekdays.
places.health: The summit area is ~2,300–2,500 m; the highest peak (Fenghuangshan, 2,572 m) is off-limits. Fine as a day visit.
